chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
If a man sees what he dislikes in his dream, let him turn over to the other side from the side on which he was sleeping.
Indeed, the whispering is from Satan, to grieve those who believe, but he will not harm them except by permission of Allah.

Then let him say: I seek refuge with what the closely neared angels of Allah, and His prophets, and His righteous servants sought refuge with, from the evil of what I saw, and from the evil of the castaway Satan.

key_terms.مَلَائِكَةُ اللَّهِ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ: The closely neared angels of Allah

ai.seo_question: What should one do and say after seeing an unpleasant dream according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi outlines a comprehensive spiritual remedy for negative dreams, emphasizing the transition from physical discomfort to spiritual protection. It integrates the Quranic concept of 'Najwa' (Satan's secret whispers) with a specific supplication invoking the refuge of the Maqarrun (nearby angels), Anbiya (prophets), and Salihun (righteous servants), reflecting the Shia emphasis on intercession and divine protection through exemplary figures.
